title: fix(floor): move on from a defective reply (empty, cut off, prose where json was owed), as the readme promises
description:
## what

the floor walk should move on from a defective reply (empty, cut off, or prose where json was owed), as the readme promises.

## why

the readme's `floor` row: *"one endpoint per attempt; a throttle, refusal, or bad reply moves on to the next cheapest"*. in `rhachet-brains-openrouter@0.1.3` (the latest), `getOneSuppliedCompletion` runs `getOneReplyDefectError` AFTER `getOneFloorCompletion` returns. the floor walk hops only on transport throttles and refusals, so a 200 reply that is empty, cut off, or prose-where-json-was-owed throws for the whole ask while cheaper-next endpoints sit unused.

## evidence

`ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-ehmpathy` full integration run (2026-10-08) failed four `checkRetention` cases on one ask:

> `💥 MalfunctionError: openrouter returned no usable reply (finish_reason=stop, 0 chars). the host replied empty where a json schema was owed.` — provider `DekaLLM`, generation `gen-1791441176-u3hIiYCtTueyp8Os2iHQ`

the same suites pass alone (`checkRetention` + `clusterKernels`: 18/18), so one host answered empty once, and the atom gave up rather than ask the next host.

## shape

move the reply-defect check inside the floor walk:

1. a defective reply records an attempt (`{ tag, verdict: 'defect', cause }`)
2. a prose-where-json host goes into the 7-day ignore list the atom already keeps
3. the walk hops to the next qualified endpoint; only an exhausted queue throws, with every attempt listed

clamp: a stubbed endpoint list whose cheapest host answers empty and whose next answers json — the ask returns the second host's answer, and `supply.attempts` names both.

callers should not wrap the ask in a retry; that would mask the next host-level defect too.
